prerequisites: Successful completion of all other courses in the degree program is required for the final evaluation and inclusion of the Bachelor's Thesis grade in the academic records.

learning_outcomes.text: Original individual work to be presented and defended before a university tribunal, consisting of a project in the field of specific Industrial Engineering technologies of a professional nature, synthesizing and integrating the competencies acquired in the studies.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering whose objective is, in accordance with the knowledge acquired as established in section 5 of order CIN/351/2009, the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Ability to manage the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply the principles and methods of quality.
Ability of organization and planning in the business environment, and other institutions and organizations.

teaching_methods: Information and knowledge transmission through the Virtual Course
Specific methodology for each Bachelor's Thesis determined by its characteristics
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by the Director's evaluation report (25%) and the individual evaluation reports from each of the three Tribunal members (25% each). To receive a final grade for the Bachelor's Thesis, all other courses in the degree program must be successfully completed. Accreditation of a B1 English level (via official academic certification) is also required. The defense itself consists of a presentation (max 30 minutes) and a debate with the Tribunal (max 30 minutes).
institution: Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia
